Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Technique work on material and process experimentation. Technique: test a material or mark-making process through material and process experimentation, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Set criteria before making and evaluate observable evidence against them.
primary_task: Target for this apply session: Apply material and process experimentation independently to an unfamiliar case. Communicate understanding of material and process experimentation using subject-appropriate evidence or representation. Check, revise, or improve the work on material and process experimentation against the stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: State your result for material and process experimentation and the single strongest piece of evidence supporting it. What material and process experimentation means here: A studio technique is a repeatable material action used on purpose, not a required personal style. 1. Independent creation: Create a fresh, bounded work involving material and process experimentation. State an intent, choose at least two relevant relationships, preserve one intermediate state, check the result, and make or deliberately decline one revision with a reason. 2. Critique: Describe before judging. Locate evidence, compare it with the maker’s stated intent, ask one genuine question, and offer options; the maker keeps final authority. A private self-critique receives full credit. 3. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. Your choices remain yours: Different subject, safe material route, mark or construction vocabulary, degree of finish, revision that serves the stated intent choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about material and process experimentation, and it belongs to "Advanced Studio Practice and Personal Direction", which also covers separate topics such as sustained observational and interpretive drawing. Close out with this check before you stop: State your result for material and process experimentation and the single strongest piece of evidence supporting it. At grade 9 the bar is independent work with explicit criteria set before you start, and evidence that you evaluated the finished result against those criteria rather than against how it felt.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a labelled visual, tactile, constructed, or accessible digital work to preserve the making target; prose alone does not claim visual or material technique evidence. You may describe the work in writing and have one trusted adult verify a physical artifact without photographing you or your home. No microphone, camera, or recording is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting material and process experimentation.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce material and process experimentation to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one tool pressure relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact tool pressure evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from tool pressure, direction, layering, joining, edge, surface, proportion, and safe control; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply material and process experimentation under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on material and process experimentation rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What material and process experimentation means here
concept_instruction.body: A studio technique is a repeatable material action used on purpose, not a required personal style.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: Pressure, angle, speed, sequence, moisture, layering, or joining changes the visible and tactile result; isolating one variable makes cause and effect easier to notice.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: More control can increase clarity, while a looser action may preserve energy or texture. The useful choice depends on intent and safe material limits. Worked example: Three short studies that change only pressure reveal which marks stay light, become dark, or damage the surface. Non-example: Copying a polished image without recording setup, actions, and changes hides the technique the lesson is meant to teach.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant tool pressure, direction, layering, joining, edge, surface, proportion, and safe control.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in material and process experimentation.
technique_sequence.why: Pressure, angle, speed, sequence, moisture, layering, or joining changes the visible and tactile result; isolating one variable makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for material and process experimentation is present, but the record does not yet locate tool pressure, direction, layering, joining, edge, surface, proportion, and safe control that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
